ctx.x: Some of them…when you were born in the South, you know what to expect. Born in the North, naturally you’ll go down there and do something stupid not even knowing that you’re wrong, ‘cause who’s who to say who’s right and who’s wrong. Who are they to say you can’t go in this place, you can’t do this, you got two bathrooms to go to, if you go to the white bathroom you get clubbed by the police. That’s so stupid. But there were a few musicians…Lucky Millinder got beat up down there one time. Policeman just really…he…

Yeah, Archie Hall. You can read about him in the Black Almanac. I have one. I bought it for my daughter when she was going to school. I don’t think she even looked at the first page. There’s Archie Hall, he was one of the fine trombone players of that time. He could do anything with a trombone and as I was reading about it in Europe, they went over there to play, they just absolutely amazed the people in Europe. The Jim Europe band, the 369th, they had such an organization, people were amazed at how they could…

You know, the mothers would take it upon themselves to go see whatever, they wouldn't care what it was, they would go to hell to see why your kid was being mistreated, you know. And she said, "Well, that's mistreatment. I bought you this tuxedo and you've got a new horn." And she would say, "How in the hell does he think you're going to make it in life and help me and help yourself unless you get paid? She said, "Experience, you can't eat experience, you know."

So she said, well, you just can't work no more if you are just going to work for experience. So he finally started paying me 35 cents a night. And this band was -- this guy named Archie White, trombone player, oh, he was -- everybody, Lawrence Brown knows him. He was a fantastic trombone player.
